chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakil narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: Abu Abdillah al-Jamurani narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Hamzah al-Bata'ini from Mandal ibn Ali from Abi al-Sabah al-Kanani from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves from His believing servants every supplication. Therefore, you must engage in supplication from the night vigil (sahar) until sunrise, for it is a time in which the doors of heaven are opened, the winds blow, sustenance is distributed, and great needs are fulfilled.

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاء: Doors of heaven, metaphorically indicating the accessibility of divine response.
key_terms.السَّحَر: The period of night vigil or pre-dawn hours, specifically the time before Fajr prayer.
key_terms.الْأَرْزَاق: Sustenance or provisions, referring to both material and spiritual blessings distributed by God.
key_terms.الْحَوَائِج الْعِظَام: Great or major needs, referring to significant requests made by the supplicant.
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْس: Sunrise, marking the end of the recommended time for this supplication.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of supplicating between dawn and sunrise in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition from Imam al-Baqir (AS), highlighting the pre-dawn period (Sahar) as a unique window of divine acceptance where sustenance is distributed and major needs are fulfilled. This narration underscores the spiritual significance of Tahajjud and morning supplications in Shia practice, linking the physical act of waking for prayer with the metaphysical opening of heavenly gates. It serves as a practical encouragement for believers to prioritize dua during this blessed time to secure both worldly provisions and spiritual closeness to Allah.
